with_class_prior.class_prior_binding: completion enumeration order binds 0.3 to t_causes_z_no_adjustment and 0.7 to z_causes_t_adjusts_z
with_class_prior.derivation: the law is noise-free, so each completion's adjustment regression is exact on the sample: adjusting z@-1 recovers 2; without it the slope is 2 + 0.5 Cov(z@-1, t@-1) / Var(t@-1) = 3.2136 on these 800 rows; the class-prior mixture is 0.7 * 2 + 0.3 * 3.2136

temporal_pag_mixed_identification.note: Truths follow from the law: a unit pulse (or single-step sustained shift) of t at lag 1 moves y by 2; the latent z<->t completion is the one unidentified completion, so its prior mass 0.3 stays unidentified.

oracle.method: noise-free stated law: each completion's adjustment regression is exact on the sample, so the per-completion and mixture effects follow by arithmetic (see `derivation`)
oracle.formula: adjusted = 2; unadjusted = 2 + 0.5 Cov(z@-1, t@-1)/Var(t@-1) (exact least squares on the 800-row series); mixture = 0.7*2 + 0.3*unadjusted; full window = 2 + 3.
context_only_outputs: which PAG completion is unidentified (the mass 0.3 is taken from the declared prior)
oracle.independence_basis: The generator rebuilds the stated closed-form series, forms the lag-aligned design rows and solves the two least-squares problems exactly over rationals; it imports no Antecedent code and no statistics package. The shared object is the stated law.
